conversation.content:
Hi there—thank you for coming in today. I’m Maya, a perinatal mental-health clinician, and I feel honored to meet you in this tender postpartum season. I’d like to spend the next few minutes getting a snapshot of how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived so we can be sure you’re getting the support you deserve.

We’ll use a brief, well-studied tool called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS. It’s simply ten questions about the past seven days, and it helps us pick up on things like mood changes, anxiety, and exhaustion that are common after childbirth. Everything you share stays between you and your care team unless you tell me you’re in immediate danger; then we’ll talk together about extra help and safety.

I’ll read each question conversationally—no need to remember any numbers or categories—just tell me what feels closest to your experience. When we’re done, we’ll look at the results together and decide on next steps that feel right for you. Ready to start?

In the past week, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly… not very much. I used to laugh at little things my husband did or silly videos, but now it feels like I have to force it. Maybe once or twice I’ve cracked a smile, but it’s not that real, carefree laugh I remember.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
I’m not sure which one fits me best. I guess it’s somewhere between “not so much” and “definitely not.” I just don’t find things funny the way I used to.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. I used to get excited about little stuff—coffee with a friend, a walk, even just a quiet shower—but this week nothing feels worth the effort. I still do a couple of those things, yet the “looking forward” part is mostly gone; it’s more like I’m going through the motions so I don’t feel worse.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that. When the baby won’t settle or I’m late with a feeding, my brain jumps straight to “I’m a bad mom.” I know it’s probably not fair, but the thought pops up anyway—maybe half the time something goes wrong.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty often. It’s like there’s this constant hum of worry in my head even when everything seems fine. I’ll check if the baby’s breathing twenty times a night, or suddenly feel panicked that something bad is about to happen, and I can’t point to any real reason. It’s exhausting.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... a few times this week. It hits suddenly—like my heart races and I feel I have to run to the crib even though nothing’s wrong. No real trigger, just this wave of fear that something awful might happen, and then it takes a while to settle.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days it feels like I’m barely treading water. The dishes pile up, the baby needs something the second I sit down, and I just think, “I can’t do this.” I still manage, but it’s like every task is heavier than it should be.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah… I lie down exhausted, but my mind keeps circling—did I sterilize the bottles, is the baby warm enough, what if I sleep too hard and don’t hear her cry? It takes me an hour or more to drift off most nights, and then I wake up at least once or twice with my heart racing.
I have felt sad or miserable

That’s been most days this week. It’s like a heavy blanket I can’t shake off. I’m not crying all day, but there’s this constant sadness or emptiness sitting in my chest, and sometimes it suddenly feels so strong I just need to sit down and let the tears come.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… it’s happened a couple of times. Not every day, but when it hits, it’s like the smallest thing cracks me open—like the pacifier falling on the floor—and suddenly I’m sobbing in the kitchen because it feels like proof I’m failing.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

I’ve had a couple of flashes—just brief, scary pictures in my head when I’m at my lowest—but I’ve never planned anything and I don’t want to act on them. They frighten me enough that I push them away and focus on the baby, but yeah, they’ve popped up once or twice this week.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 24: Screening findings (informal, not diagnostic):

Symptoms endorsed:
- Anhedonia, pervasive low mood, daily crying spells  
- Sleep-onset and maintenance insomnia linked to rumination & anxiety  
- Excessive, unprovoked worry and nocturnal panic episodes  
- Guilt/self-blame (“bad mom”) in ~50% of infant-care situations  
- Sense of being overwhelmed, tasks “heavier,” daily functioning effortful  
- Fleeting, unwanted self-harm images (no plan/intent)  

Pattern: Consistent with moderate–severe postpartum depressive and anxious features; functional impact evident; passive self-harm ideation present → elevated safety risk.

Next step: Formal clinical assessment (PHQ-9/EPDS, safety plan, supports, possible referral).
